newsitem.title: USA: US spot products up in thin trade, tracking NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US spot products up in thin trade, tracking NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot product prices firmed by the close Tuesday in thin trading, as the nearby NYMEX prices extended the sharp gains seen the previous day.

NYMEX prices surged during the afternoon, helped by concerns that the strike at France's Elf Aquitaine would spread to other oil companies there. Union workers began the strike six days ago at three refineries, crippling about a quarter of that nation's output.
Activity in the spot markets remained subdued, with few deals finalized, traders said, and most participants sitting on the sidelines.

New York Harbor (NYH) gasoline prices became clearer Tuesday, after Monday's murky talk. Prompt unleaded M5 barrels in the Harbor were put at about 3.50 to 3.75 cents over the screen, while the reformulated (RFG) A5 87-octane was quoted between 5.00 to 5.50 cents over.
Premium conventional and reformulated material in NYH remained very strong, with buyers forced to chase prices higher in thin conditions, according to traders.
U.S. Gulf conventional unleaded for prompt delivery hovered near the recent levels, sitting at about 2.00 cents under NYMEX, while A4 RFG gasoline was put at 2.25 cents over.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
